rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a TiN interlayer beneath a Cr coating, whereas the target paper uses a compositionally varied AlTiCrZrNbTa high-entropy alloy coating without any interlayer; these are fundamentally different interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions subcritical water (~300°C) and high-temperature steam up to 1200°C, while the target paper tests isothermal oxidation in flowing steam at 1000°C and 1100°C; the regimes overlap only in the high-temperature steam aspect, but the specific temperatures and the inclusion of subcritical water differ.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis relies on a TiN diffusion barrier to inhibit Cr–Zr interdiffusion, whereas the target paper's mechanism involves Al content tuning to form a protective Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 oxide layer and avoid detrimental intermetallics; these are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced interdiffusion and maintained oxidation resistance for a Cr/TiN system, while the target paper predicts and measures an optimal Al content for oxidation resistance in an AlTiCrZrNbTa coating; the predicted property (oxidation resistance) is the same, but the system and specific outcome differ.
